Name: Gradual Seasons
Author: opoiuuuu
Description:
Description

In Stardew Valley the whole world switches season at once: you go to bed in fall and wake up to a completely white map. Gradual Seasons blends the seasons into each other instead.

In the last week of each season, the next one slowly creeps in. Patches of snow settle across the ground through late fall, trees drop their leaves and gather snow, snow builds up on your roofs, and rainy days start turning into snow days. By the last day of fall most of the valley already looks like winter, so the change on day 1 is a small step instead of a jump. The old season then lingers for the first few days of the new one, and the same thing happens at every season change: fall colours spread through late summer, and in late winter the snow melts away in patches as spring grass and blossoms break through.

The mod uses the game’s own seasonal art, so everything looks like Stardew Valley. It follows the in-game date, nothing extra is saved, and you can add or remove it at any time.

Installation instructions

Install the latest version of SMAPI (https://smapi.io) and start the game through SMAPI once.
Optional: install Generic Mod Config Menu to change the settings in game.
Download Gradual Seasons and unzip it into your game’s Mods folder. You should end up with Mods/GradualSeasons/manifest.json.
Start the game through SMAPI. Gradual Seasons should be in the list of loaded mods in the SMAPI console.

To change the settings, use Generic Mod Config Menu, or edit Mods/GradualSeasons/config.json (created the first time you start the game).

To update, replace the GradualSeasons folder (keep your config.json if you changed it). To uninstall, delete the folder; nothing is left behind in your save.

Main features

The map changes gradually

The game’s own next-season tiles appear in natural patches, with soft edges that don’t follow the tile grid: snowy ground, frosted cliffs and pond banks, snowy town roofs and big map trees.
Late fall: snow settles a little more each day. Late winter: the thaw, with spring grass and blossoms breaking through. Late summer: fall’s orange ground creeps in. Late spring: summer’s ground spreads.
Ponds, rivers and the sea slowly change colour together, under the game’s moving water.
Stone paths stay clear of snow a little longer and lose it first.
The same spots keep their new look as the patches grow, so nothing flickers from day to day.

Trees change bit by bit

Wild trees (oak, maple, pine and mahogany) change in leaf-sized clumps: leaves turn orange and red through late summer, drop and gather snow through late fall, and bud through late winter.

Snow on your roofs

The game gives farm buildings no winter look. With this mod, snow builds up on the roofs of the farmhouse, cabins, barns, coops, sheds and stable through late fall, stays all winter and melts in early spring.
The silo, well, mill, slime hutch and shipping bin get a cap of snow along their top.
Painted buildings work too: the snow stays white on top of your paint.

Weather particles and ground details

Snow flurries on dry days in late fall, getting heavier each day, and sleet over the rain.
Falling autumn leaves in late summer and early winter, and cherry petals in early summer.
Fallen leaves, petals and summer wildflowers on the ground.
Particles never double up what the game is already showing, fade in and out smoothly, and are dimmer at night.

The weather follows along

Late fall: rain and storms may turn to snow, and clear days sometimes bring early snow. Late winter: snow may turn to rain as the thaw starts. Early spring: the odd late cold snap. Late spring and late summer: storms build and calm.
The chance grows each day, so full snow days are most likely right before winter.
Only the main player’s game changes the forecast, the same way a Rain Totem does, so the TV forecast and multiplayer stay in sync.
The forecast is never changed for day 1 of a season, festivals, weddings, Green Rain or weather added by other mods.

Settings and commands

Turn every part on or off, choose how many days a season creeps in (0 to 14) and lingers (0 to 7), and how strong the changes are.
Console commands: gs_status shows what the mod is doing today, and gs_preview <season> <day> previews another date’s map and particles (for example gs_preview fall 28).
The map changes also show up in the game’s own map screenshots.

Requirements

Stardew Valley 1.6 or later
SMAPI 4.0 or later
Generic Mod Config Menu (optional, for changing the settings in game)

Multiplayer: every player who wants to see the changes needs the mod. Only the host’s copy changes the weather.

Good to know

A snow day doesn’t water your crops (just like in vanilla winter). When late-fall rain turns into snow, water your crops yourself.
Ginger Island, the Desert, indoor areas and festivals keep their normal look.
Fruit trees and bushes still change on day 1 of the season.

Compatibility

Works with map mods and recolours, since it uses whatever seasonal art your game has loaded.
If another mod already gives your buildings a winter look, turn off “Snow on roofs”.
If you use another weather mod, you can turn off “Change the weather” and keep everything else.
